record.original_question: Is the following conjecture true? Conjecture A100. (i) (raised on Nov. 2, 2009 via a message to Number Theory List) If n > 1 is an odd integer satisfying the Morley congruence ( n − 1 (n − 1)/ 2 ) ≡ (−1)(n−1)/ 24n−1 (mod n3), 76 ZHI-WEI SUN then n must be a prime. (ii) ([S10]) If an odd integer n > 1 satisfies the congruence n−1∑ k=0 (2k k ) 2k ≡ (−1)(n−1)/ 2 (mod n2), then n must be a prime. (iii) ([S11j]) Set an := ∑ n k=0 (n k ) 2 Ck for n = 0 , 1, 2, . . . . Any integer n > 1 satisfying a1 + · · · + an−1 ≡ 0 (mod n2) must be a prime.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Decide whether each of the following three converse-type primality criteria holds.

(i) Let $n > 1$ be an odd integer such that
$$\binom{n-1}{(n-1)/2} \equiv (-1)^{(n-1)/2}\, 4^{n-1} \pmod{n^3}.$$
Must $n$ necessarily be prime?

(ii) Let $n > 1$ be an odd integer such that
$$\sum_{k=0}^{n-1} \binom{2k}{k}\, 2^k \equiv (-1)^{(n-1)/2} \pmod{n^2}.$$
Must $n$ necessarily be prime?

(iii) For $m = 0, 1, 2, \ldots$ define
$$a_m \;=\; \sum_{k=0}^{m} \binom{m}{k}^{2} C_k,$$
where $C_k = \frac{1}{k+1}\binom{2k}{k}$ is the $k$-th Catalan number. Let $n > 1$ be an integer such that
$$a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_{n-1} \equiv 0 \pmod{n^2}.$$
Must $n$ necessarily be prime?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a published proof or disproof of the three converse primality criteria (Morley-type congruence mod n^3, central binomial sum congruence mod n^2, and Catalan-Franel-type sum congruence mod n^2). Related supercongruences of Z.-W. Sun have been proved for primes, but the converse statements (that any composite n satisfying the congruence cannot exist) appear not to be settled in the located literature.
